zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 7; they obstruct the downward view from Decks 8, 9, and 10, with Deck 8 most affected and obstruction lessening as you go higher.
zones.effect: You'll see the boat deck and tenders below instead of open water straight down, though the horizon view remains clear; this matters for photographers and those who want an unobstructed sight line to the waterline.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who want a fully open ocean view or to watch port operations; doesn't matter to those focused on horizon views, sunsets, or privacy (the boats actually shield you from being seen from the pier).

zones.what: Mid-ship balconies on Decks 9, 10, and 11 cantilever outboard past the lifeboat line, creating wider balconies with side views along the hull.
zones.effect: These balconies are wider and offer better side-to-side views compared to standard balconies elsewhere; they sit low and central where motion is minimal, and typically price lower than higher decks despite the extra space.
zones.mattersTo: Value hunters and those who prioritize space and stability over height; these are among the best balcony deals on the ship for people who understand the geometry.

zones.what: Deck 16 sits directly above Deck 15 forward, both dedicated MSC Yacht Club decks with cabins and likely YC-exclusive outdoor space on 16.
zones.effect: Minimal impact as both decks are Yacht Club and share the same guest profile; any foot traffic above is limited to YC guests accessing their own cabins or private areas.
zones.mattersTo: Low concern; Yacht Club guests on 15 should expect comparable activity patterns overhead.

zones.what: Deck 8 below houses the Panorama Lounge (forward) and portions of the promenade and shopping area (mid-ship), which operate into evening hours.
zones.effect: Some music, foot traffic, and ambient noise from entertainment and shopping venues directly below, particularly evenings; not a nightclub-level issue but more active than a cabin-over-cabin scenario.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers in forward and mid-ship Deck 9 should consider this; aft Deck 9 sits over more cabins and public spaces that close earlier.

zones.what: Deck 16 mid and aft areas contain the main pool deck, including two main pools, whirlpools, and the Atmosphere Pool Bar, active from early morning through late evening.
zones.effect: Pool deck activity directly overhead means daytime and evening foot traffic, deck chair dragging, music, and pool sounds; this continues until the pools close around 10-11 PM.
zones.mattersTo: Deck 15 cabins exist only forward, so this doesn't affect guest cabins directly; included for completeness as the pool deck geography is important for understanding Decks 14 and below.

zones.what: The Top Sail Lounge occupies Deck 15 forward directly below Deck 16 cabins, operating as an observation lounge and bar.
zones.effect: Lounge activity below during daytime and evening hours; generally quieter than a nightclub but not silent, with music and conversation filtering up.
zones.mattersTo: Yacht Club guests on Deck 16 seeking absolute silence may notice some ambient sound from below in evenings; those unbothered by muted lounge atmosphere won't care.

zones.what: Deck 15 mid and aft house the buffet (Marketplace) and related dining venues that operate from early breakfast through late-night snacks.
zones.effect: Buffet activity overhead means foot traffic, chair movement, and kitchen sounds from roughly 6 AM to midnight or later; this is one of the busiest public venues on the ship.
zones.mattersTo: Anyone in mid or aft Deck 14 should expect this; light sleepers and those wanting quiet mornings should avoid these sections, while those who sleep through noise or are rarely in the cabin won't mind.

zones.what: Aft cabins on the lowest guest decks (5 and 8) sit closest to the engine room and propulsion machinery.
zones.effect: Low-frequency vibration and hum, particularly noticeable when engines are working hard during maneuvering or rough seas; modern MSC dampening reduces but doesn't eliminate it.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive guests should avoid these; those who sleep through white noise or wear earplugs often don't notice, and the aft location offers other benefits like closer proximity to aft entertainment.

zones.what: Forward Deck 5 sits near bow thrusters, which activate during docking and maneuvering in port.
zones.effect: Loud thruster noise during port arrivals and departures, typically early morning and late afternoon; the sound is intense but brief, lasting minutes rather than hours.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to anyone who wants to sleep through port days; doesn't matter if you're up early anyway or appreciate the operational sounds as part of the experience.

zones.what: Primary crew corridor access points are typically located at the forward and aft ends of each cabin deck, where crew enter guest corridors from service areas.
zones.effect: Increased crew foot traffic in these zones during service hours (early morning room service, evening turndown, overnight cleaning shifts); doors may close audibly and you'll see crew coming and going.
zones.mattersTo: Cabins at the extreme forward or aft ends of corridors may notice more activity; mid-ship cabins are typically quieter from this perspective.
